objective: A frozen exploratory census, exact: for every orientably regular map of genus at least 2 of the earlier roster (seen in a pilot) and of seven groups not read before (PSL(2,31), PSL(2,37), PGL(2,17), PGL(2,19), SL(2,11), GL(2,7), S7), how each ring's closest contacts are reached from a target contact (all by one route, one route and a tie, ties only), with the frozen hypotheses H1 (every on-time map has, at every ring, a closest contact reached by one route) and H2 (every map whose diameter is at most its first tie plus 2 is on time) tested on the new groups.
status: Closed: supported 2026-11-09 (exploratory, exact; frozen contract pre-registered in dee5004a4): on seven groups not read before (PSL(2,31), PSL(2,37), PGL(2,17), PGL(2,19), SL(2,11), GL(2,7), S7), every one of the 77 on-time maps of genus at least 2 (of 1,056) has, at every ring, a closest contact reached by a single shortest route (H1, no counterexample); on the earlier roster the one exception is a map of S6 of type (6,6), genus 61, whose two rings are rescued by counts 2, 2, 3. H2 (shallow ties are harmless) holds but was vacuous on the new roster.
title: How on-time maps of higher genus reach their rings: a census
